title: Income and Racial Shifts in Minnesota
abstract: An interactive Shiny project exploring personal income trends from 2012 to 2022 alongside changes in Minnesota’s racial and ethnic population composition. County- and census-tract-level views bring public datasets into a shared geographic interface.
introduction: How do shifts in racial and ethnic population demographics correlate with income changes across Minnesota counties over the past decade? We aimed to explore how economic gaps among racial and ethnic groups might affect income levels and access to economic opportunities. By doing so, we hope to highlight economic challenges faced by diverse communities and provide insights for policies that promote inclusion and equity.
output: Introduction Tab - An animated GIF showing changes in per capita income per county over time.
County-level Analysis Tab - Interactive county map with income and racial changes from 2012–2022. Slider for controlling visualization pace.
Tract-level Analysis Tab - Similar to county-level, but at census tract scale.
Income Trend Plot - Grey lines for all counties, highlighted blue line for the selected county.
Racial Makeup Trend Plot - Trends in racial composition for the selected county.
further_research: Role of job availability and sector-specific income growth in shaping income disparities.
ethical_considerations: County- and tract-level patterns describe places, not individual outcomes. They do not establish income differences within racial groups.
Interpreting income changes requires checking the measure, units, and whether values are inflation-adjusted.
The dashboard is descriptive; it does not establish that demographic change caused income change, or attribute year-to-year movements to a particular economic policy.
